title: Prometheus’ Architecture
text:
The Prometheus’ Architecture is a foundational framework for a metamathematical reasoning system. It is designed to contain the expressive power of ZFC set theory while bridging the reasoning levels of rigorous mathematical logic and human-level reasoning. The architecture is built upon a set of primitives and constructions that allow for the representation and manipulation of mathematical objects and concepts.




Sets (constant, variable-constant, and variable. The program will attempt to classify everything in terms of constant or variable sets)

Constant type set: {}C (represents a collection as a single object)
Variable-constant type set: {}VC (represents a possibility space of an unknown single object)
Variable type set: {}V (represents a collection of objects as an abstraction over all members of the collection)

1Programming language primitives

String
Integer
Boolean
etc.

A∩B = {x | x∈A and x∈B}C



Union

A∪B = {x | x∈A or x∈B}C



Power Set

𝒫(A) = {X | X⊆A}C



Predicate Subset

{x | P(x)}C = {x | x∈A and P(x)}C



Cartesian Product

A×B = {(a,b) | a∈A and b∈B}C



Function Mapping

f(A) = {f(x) | x∈A}C As well as extending set theory formulations that build up set theory constructively:



Disjoint Union

A⊎B = {AX{0}C ∪ BX{1}C}C



Relation

R⊆A×B = { (a,b) | a∈A and b∈B }C



Function

f:A→B = { (a,b) | a∈A and b∈B and f(a)=b }C *with the additional constraint that for all a∈A, there exists a unique b∈B such that (a,b)∈f; that is, one input maps to only one output


etc.






Impossibility:

NA = {}VC



Tautology/Single possibility:

x = {x}VC



Possibility compilation:

{A={…}VC, B={…}VC}VC = {AUB}VC



Ambiguous Component:

f({…}VC) = {f(…)}VC – A VC set with type X members can be used as a component in any construction, object method, or operation that requires a type X member. Operation and object method results will be a VC set as a collection of evaluation outcomes for each member. E.g. {3, 4}%3 = {0,1} E.g. length({“12”, 12}) = {2, NA}














Set-typing; indicates membership of a constant or subsetting of constant-variable or variable sets in relation to the Constant “type” set. Useful for defining allowed domains and behaviors. Adds “types” but in a more intuitive approach, allowing a term to belong to multiple types. X is of settype A means: X is a Constant as a member of A or X is either a VC set or variable set as a subset of A.

title: Prometheus’ Architecture Documentation
text:
Starting Axioms and Template Structures:

Axioms


Starting Template Structures
Progression Axioms: 1. Some first object exists (e.g., 0) 2. Every object has a successor, which is also an object. 3. No two objects have the same successor 4. The first object is not the successor of any object. 5. If a property is possessed by the first object and also by the successor of every object that has that property, then it is possessed by all objects (including classifications and memberships).
This is a generalization of Peano’s Axioms: 1. 0 is a number. 2. Every number has a successor, which is also a number. 3. No two numbers have the same successor 4. 0 is not the successor of any number. 5. If a property is possessed by 0 and also by the successor of every number that has that property, then it is possessed by all numbers. * Endless sequence of unique numbers (via 2 and 3) that don’t loop (via 4), which includes all numbers (via 5). * “Ordinal arithmetic” – m+n is defined using m+0=m and m+(n+1)=S(m+n), reducing recursion. Defines addition and equivalents for progressions.

Some mechanism of mapping between sets to compare their cardinality, allowing the definition of numbers as equivalence classes of sets with equal cardinality. (One-one relation identification with the two sets as domain and codomain.) pdf pg 37

[Number as defined by collection of equivalence classes of sets with equal cardinality]
Peanos’ Axioms and/or Frege’s Axioms Predicates as functions that map to truth values

To Do and Future Work

Top Priority

Explore the “environment” concept with Claude to understand how a program might be an agent according to my perspective, and how to implement this in Prometheus.
Finalize axioms for numbers systems, (e.g., Peano’s axioms, Frege’s axioms)
Explicitly define axioms for relations (equivalence, partial order, strict partial order, etc.) and mappings, enabling checking for equal cardinality of sets (allowing the “number” abstraction to be defined as a set of equivalence classes of sets with equal cardinality?).
Define axioms for predicates, including quantifiers and logical connectives (and, or, not, implies, etc.) and how they relate to the custom set types (constant, variable-constant, variable).
Define incomplete extensional definitions with unknown unknowns, and how they relate to the custom set types (constant, variable-constant, variable). Note: define as an unknown that aligns with known (an unknown from the category of possibilities defined by a known detail). Only unknown unknowns with no known details are impossible to define.
Define attributes by their relationships to other objects and their possible values, and explore abstraction with attributes and how they relate to the custom set types (constant, variable-constant, variable). ### Next Priority
Define axioms for functions, including injective, surjective, bijective, and other properties
Define axioms for the custom set types (constant, variable-constant, variable) and their relationships to each other and to standard set theory.
Explore tests for determining cardinality of sets, including finite, countably infinite, and uncountably infinite sets (allowing explicit exhaustive enumeration of possibilities for sufficiently small finite sets).

I want a constraint solver that will solve scheduling problems for several people over 15 min time slots. More people or positions can be added as needed. People and positions can be defined with various attributes used for constaints (e.g. “Male” and “Female” people, “Physically demanding” positions, etc.) that can be used to define rules. The program should support rules for people, positions, and time slots in any combination (e.g. “Person A cannot be scheduled for Position B during Time Slot C”) or any generalization (e.g. Person A cannot have Position B, ever). Rules can be marked as required, preferred, or inactive (ignored during checks and solving), and the program will fill in the schedule as a table-like chart with time on the x-axis (at the top) and people on the y-axis (on the left) with all the assignments required by the required rules, and faded suggestions for the preferred rules. The main schedule chart will be on the left, and a list of the most possibility-reducing decisions will be on the right, with the most possibility-reducing decisions at the top and any rules that are currently violated above them in the list with a red outline. Below both the main schedule chart and the list of decisions will be a list of all the rules, with the required rules at the top and the preferred rules below them. When a time slot is selected there should be a dropdown of all positions, with positions that align with preferred rules marked with a star and positions currently forbidden by required rules as grayed out, and when you hover your mouse over them the contradicting rule will be displayed as a hover window and the appropriate areas on the chart will be outlined in red. The rules list should have search and filter options to display only rules that 1. deal with a time constraint, person constraint, or position constraint in general as a specific constraint (e.g. “Person A cannot be scheduled for Position B” has a person and a position being specifically constrained), 2. are required or preferred, and 3. rules that deal with specific times, people, or positions. There should be a gear icon for advanced settings that opens a menu from which users can define new positions, classifying tags, and rules. When positions are defined they are assigned a length of time which must be fit into the schedule (e.g. a position that is 30 minutes long will take up two 15 minute time slots and someone can’t be scheduled for it for a single time slot). An implicit built-in rule is that no person can be scheduled for more than one position at a time, but a position can be scheduled for more than one person at a time unless it is checked as a “single-person” position when it is defined. Rules can also have tags that can be used to group them together for searching and filtering. The program should have a “solve” button that will attempt to fill in the schedule as much as possible while satisfying all required rules and as many preferred rules as possible. Positions should have color-coding options in the advanced settings that will be displayed in the main schedule chart, with faded versions of the colors displayed for preferred rules’ suggestions that haven’t been selected yet. If a suggestion is clicked on their should be a small popup with a “accept” and “reject button” – if accepted the suggestion will be added to the schedule and the chart will be updated, and if rejected the suggestion will be removed visually from the chart (but the preferred rule that spurred the suggestion will remain in the rules list, unaffected). The default program should have 10:30 to 4:30 as the time range (24 time slots), but this can be changed in the advanced settings. The program should have save and load buttons that will save the current schedule as a formatted excel file and load a schedule from a formatted excel file, respectively.
